back: A description of how a company creates, delivers and captures value: who its customers are, what it offers, how it reaches them, how it earns revenue and what it costs to operate.

front: List the key elements of a business model.
back: Value proposition, customer segments, channels, revenue model and pricing, cost structure and operating model, and key resources and partners.

B2C sells to consumers (many small transactions, brand matters). B2B sells to businesses (fewer, larger customers, longer sales cycles, concentration risk). B2G sells to governments (procurement rules, long contracts).
A cheap base product builds an installed base, and the company earns most of its profit on repeat sales of high-margin consumables (for example printers and ink).

front: What is a platform business model and its key advantage?
back: It connects two or more user groups and earns a take rate, fees or advertising. Network effects make it more valuable as users join, and marginal cost per transaction is low. Reaching critical mass is costly.

front: What is operating leverage and how is DOL calculated?
back: Operating leverage is the degree to which costs are fixed. DOL = %change in EBIT / %change in sales = Q(P - V) / [Q(P - V) - F].
Fixed costs / (Price - Variable cost per unit) = fixed costs / contribution margin per unit.

front: How do you estimate expected customer lifetime and LTV in a subscription model?
back: Lifetime is approximately 1 / churn rate. LTV (simple) = gross profit per period x expected lifetime. LTV/CAC and payback period (CAC / monthly gross profit) show whether growth creates value.

front: Why can subscription models have negative working capital?
back: Customers often pay in advance, creating deferred (unearned) revenue. The firm holds the cash before delivering the service.

Asset-light models (platforms, software, franchisors) need little capital and tend to have high returns on capital and flexible costs. Capital-intensive models (utilities, airlines, steel) need heavy capex, have high fixed costs, higher operating leverage and greater sensitivity to demand.
